title: S0191 (124th General Assembly): Clerks and magistrates report to SLED case dispositions

other_topics: judicial-transparency: SECTION 1 (Section 14-17-325), SECTION 2 (new Section 22-1-200), SECTION 3 (new Section 14-25-250) — clerks, magistrates and municipal judges must report the disposition of every criminal case to SLED within ten days, not only gun cases

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2020-12-09; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess124_2021-2022/prever/191_20201209.htm (LegiScan doc 2220424))

Section 1 changed the case-disposition deadline from thirty days (struck) to ten days, weekends and holidays excluded (the 10-day disposition reporting is not quoted). Judgment call on multi: the all-cases disposition reporting is general criminal-records reporting.

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (Section 14-17-325): (B) The clerk of court shall report to the State Law Enforcement Division, within forty-eight hours, the issuance of any: (1) restraining orders; (2) orders of protection; (3) orders preventing a person from possessing a firearm; (4) convictions related to or orders issued to prevent acts of domestic violence against another person; (5) orders issued related to the stalking, intimidation, or harassment of another person; or (6) orders for bond with any limitations listed in this section.
SECTION 2 (new Section 22-1-200): (B) Magistrates shall report to the State Law Enforcement Division, within forty-eight hours, the issuance of any: (1) restraining orders; (2) orders of protection; (3) orders preventing a person from possessing a firearm; (4) convictions related to or orders issued to prevent acts of domestic violence against another person; (5) orders issued or convictions related to, or to prevent, the stalking, intimidation, or harassment of another person; or (6) orders for bond with any limitations listed in this section.
SECTION 3 (new Section 14-25-250): (B) A municipal judge shall report to the State Law Enforcement Division, within forty-eight hours, the issuance of any: (1) restraining orders; (2) orders of protection; (3) orders preventing a person from possessing a firearm; (4) convictions related to or orders issued to prevent acts of domestic violence against another person; (5) convictions related to or orders issued to prevent, the stalking, intimidation, or harassment of another person; or (6) orders for bond with any limitations listed in this section.
SECTION 4 (new Section 23-1-250): (A) Each law enforcement agency must report to the State Law Enforcement Division within twenty-four hours: (1) the filing of an order of protection, restraining order, or any order or report relating to an incident of domestic violence; (2) any incident in which a person may be prohibited from obtaining or possessing a firearm by state or federal law.
